links.outcome: Patient-level interrun stability of M-LLM diagnoses across repeated runs
links.effect: Patient-level interrun stability was low (2% to 39%) across the five M-LLMs.
links.quote: Patient-level interrun stability was low (2% to 39%), and per-case costs varied 15-fold ($0.004-$0.060) without correlation to accuracy (P > 0.05).

links.outcome: Demographic subgroup bias in M-LLM diagnostic performance
links.effect: Significant demographic biases detected, including age-related shortcut learning in pseudophakia misclassification and sex disparities in Meibomian gland dysfunction diagnosis.
links.quote: Significant demographic biases were detected, including age-related shortcut learning in pseudophakia misclassification and sex disparities in Meibomian gland dysfunction diagnosis.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of multiple multimodal LLMs for diagnostic accuracy, safety, and demographic bias on ocular surface disease clinical cases, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
